title: This Ridiculously Simple Business Makes Him $4M/Year (Can’t Fail)
promo_conflict: Ian also owns Black Op Digital, which sells marketing and outbound-sales services to security guard agencies, so the discussion overlaps with promotion of that business; no paid sponsorship is stated.

stated_problem.quote: people walk by and they'll do smash and grabs, they'll loiter, they'll cause a ruckus

idea.name: Contract security guard services
idea.one_liner: Staff licensed guards for businesses and institutions through recurring contracts and event coverage, billing for guard hours and coverage.
idea.customer: Businesses and institutions that need on-site security, access control, or event coverage.
idea.offer: Recruit, license, schedule, supervise, and provide security guards; the service also includes site procedures, training, monitoring, and some access-control technology.
idea.revenue_model: Hourly or shift-based guard contracts, event staffing, and related security services.

acquisition_channels.details: Called facilities managers, directors of security, and property managers; sometimes sent a letter or packet first and called at the time stated.
Used LinkedIn to identify and connect with property managers and collect email addresses; the transcript does not clearly say what kind of outreach was sent to those addresses.
Pursued proposals and RFPs, including school walkthroughs and event contracts.
A friend connected him to the Winter Lantern Festival, and an industry contact referred a bank client.
Built contacts through the Staten Island Chamber of Commerce and community relationships.
Used event videos on the company website, YouTube, and social media as proof in proposals.
Built an in-house SEO team and used search optimization to generate business.
The company spends on Google Ads as part of its marketing.

ideas.delivery: The company recruits and schedules licensed guards, covers shifts and callouts, trains and supervises them, monitors posts, and provides them at client sites and events. Ian described 24-hour dispatch and some custom access-control technology as part of the service.
ideas.other_uk_rules: For a UK version, guards would need the appropriate SIA licences; supplying temporary guards may bring the Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003 into scope. For prospecting, follow PECR and UK GDPR: screen live calls against TPS/CTPS, and under this brief limit cold email to limited companies with an opt-out. Consumer subscription rules under the DMCC Act do not appear central to these B2B contracts.
